title: Ethiopian Spinach Stew
community: Urban Ethiopia — the spinach stew of modern kitchens
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Spinach Stew — baby spinach or fresh spinach cooked with onion, garlic, turmeric, and tomato in the Ethiopian style. A modern addition to the Ethiopian vegetable repertoire — faster-cooking than collard greens, ideal for urban kitchens.
longDesc: Spinach wat is the urban cook's quicker alternative to Gomen — baby spinach needs no blanching and wilts in minutes, while still absorbing the Ethiopian aromatic flavours of garlic, turmeric, and onion.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden.
Add garlic and turmeric. Stir 30 seconds.
Add spinach in batches. Stir until each batch wilts.
chefTips: Add spinach in batches — it seems like a huge amount before wilting.
Do not over-cook — spinach needs only 5 minutes total.
cookingScience: See ETH106 for green vegetable cooking science. Spinach wilts much faster than collard greens because it has no fibrous stem tissue and very high water content — the cells rupture quickly, releasing their water and collapsing.
sustainabilityTips: Spinach grows quickly and requires minimal water.
healthBenefits: Very high in iron, vitamins A, C, and K.
culturalNote: Spinach wat is modern Ethiopia's practical concession to speed — where Gomen requires blanching and longer cooking, spinach delivers green nutrition in 15 minutes for the urban working cook.
